approved: Excise Tariff Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax.
The package would ban businesses from charging unfairly high prices for key goods like electricity and gas after the carbon tax ends, and give the ACCC powers to monitor prices.
A company that breaks the new price rules could face a maximum fine of 6,471 penalty units ($1,100,070), while an individual could be fined 1,295 penalty units ($220,150).
Prohibits price exploitation for certain key goods after the carbon tax repeal.
Gives the ACCC monitoring powers over prices during the transition period.
Bans false or misleading representations about the effect of the carbon tax repeal on prices.
Businesses that supply key goods such as electricity and gas, and consumers who buy those goods.

Moved a debate management motion to conclude debate on the Clean Energy Legislation (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 and related bills by Thursday this week, arguing the election gave the coalition a mandate with 90 seats to Labor's 55, Labor's worst result since 1903.

Argued against the government's carbon tax repeal bills, saying the decade from 2001 to 2010 was the warmest on record, that Direct Action would cost households an estimated $1,200 a year without a legislated cap on emissions, and noted that under Labor wind power generation trebled and 24,000 renewable energy jobs were created.

Answered that the carbon tax cost Qantas $106 million and Virgin $45 million last financial year, and said carbon tax repeal bills already before the Senate could be passed immediately with opposition support to help airline jobs, accusing the Leader of the Opposition of favouring Qantas unions over workers.
